![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14131922/assets/aaab6cbc7c79999778438e8eda617de9e2f83f687e5a1f09a91723ef9bcbefc3.svg)

Consider the matrix $A$ and vectors $\mathbf{v}_1,\mathbf{v}_2$ shown above.
If $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_2$ are two linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda=4,$ what is the value of $a+b?$
question.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A - \lambda I) \textbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =4.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -6 & 5 \\ 6 & -8 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 5 \\ 6 & -12 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}=0 \\ 6{x}_{1}-12{x}_{2}+10{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 5 & 0 \\ 6 & -12 & 10 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, $x_2$ and $x_3$ are free variables. On the other hand, from the first equation, we obtain $x_1=2x_2-\dfrac{5}{3}x_3.$ 

Hence, the general solution is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14131922/assets/3f1806eff823455bca7d446fb5e70b918d5d36aecda08424a8902ad16ed8a66c.svg)

We now deduce the eigenvectors $\mathbf v_1$ and $\mathbf v_2\mathbin :$

- Since ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14131922/assets/c9309f0609a554365a94afbe2cc1b9e981d30e77c196189dbe44436253b1d9dc.svg) we must have that $x_2=1$ and $x_3=0.$ As a result, $a=2(1)-\dfrac 53(0)=2.$

- Since ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14131922/assets/fd6445d0847b692c8d1090f0489372ce2960bf69bcab6b1b20c35f35491470cc.svg) we must have that $x_2=0$ and $x_3=3.$ As a result, $b=2(0)-\dfrac53(3)=-5.$

Therefore, $a+b=2+(-5)=-3.$
